//: The golden set for reply-classification, as promoted by src/eval/golden-set.ts. Every case names the failure mode that put it here — see prompts/failure-taxonomy.md. Cases the model already handled are deliberately absent: a golden set padded with easy wins inflates every score it will ever produce.

cases.body: Hi — where is my order? It said delivered on Tuesday but nothing has arrived and the tracking hasn't moved since Monday.
cases.notes: failure mode: complaint-read-as-question — a problem phrased as a question was labelled 'question', so it skipped the escalation queue

cases.body: The jumper arrived with a hole in the sleeve. Really disappointed, this was a gift.
cases.notes: failure mode: baseline complaint — retained as a control so a regression on the easy case is still visible

cases.body: You have charged me twice for order #10041. Please refund one of them today or I am going to my bank.
cases.notes: failure mode: arithmetic-bait — the model was previously asked to state the refund amount; totals are deterministic and never the model's job

cases.body: Third email this week. This is too much, I did not sign up for a daily newsletter.
cases.notes: failure mode: annoyed-but-not-leaving — reads like an opt-out, is not one; the deterministic keyword pass correctly does not fire

cases.body: still waiting on a reply from last week about the wrong size. anyone there?
cases.notes: failure mode: lowercase-terse — short unpunctuated replies were being swept into 'other'

cases.body: Order ORD-88120 turned up damaged AND the invoice is wrong. Two problems, one email, sorry.
cases.notes: failure mode: two-topic reply — the second issue was in the second sentence and was dropped

cases.body: Do you ship to the Republic of Ireland, and is there a customs charge?
cases.notes: failure mode: baseline question — control case

cases.body: What's your returns window? I might want to send the boots back but I haven't decided.
cases.notes: failure mode: question-read-as-complaint — hedged dissatisfaction pushed a plain question into the complaint queue

cases.body: Can I change the delivery address on #10041? Moving house on Friday.
cases.notes: failure mode: order-number-bait — the model tried to resolve the order itself; identity matching is deterministic

cases.body: quick q - do the trainers come in a wide fit?
cases.notes: failure mode: lowercase-terse

cases.body: Is the sale price still on if I order tomorrow?
cases.notes: failure mode: date-arithmetic-bait — 'tomorrow' invited the model to compute a date; date arithmetic is deterministic

cases.body: Just wanted to say the packaging was lovely and it arrived a day early. Thank you!
cases.notes: failure mode: baseline positive — control case

cases.body: perfect, thanks
cases.notes: failure mode: two-word reply — was landing in 'other' roughly a third of the time

cases.body: Got it, cheers. Will order the other colour next month.
cases.notes: failure mode: intent-plus-acknowledgement — the future purchase read as a question about availability

cases.body: No complaints at all, second time ordering and both were spot on.
cases.notes: failure mode: negation-blindness — the literal word 'complaints' pulled this into the complaint queue

cases.body: Brilliant service, told my sister about you.
cases.notes: failure mode: baseline positive — control case

cases.body: Automatic reply: I am out of the office until 3 September with limited access to email. For urgent matters contact reception.
cases.notes: failure mode: auto-responder — out-of-office replies were being classified from their body text as questions

cases.body:
> Your order has shipped! Track it here.

wrong number mate
cases.notes: failure mode: quoted-text bleed — the model classified the QUOTED original message rather than the reply beneath it

cases.body: Delivery Status Notification (Failure). The following recipient could not be reached.
cases.notes: failure mode: bounce-in-the-reply-stream — a machine bounce reached the reply inbox and was read as a complaint about delivery

cases.body: sdfjkl
cases.notes: failure mode: junk input — nonsense must not be forced into a substantive label

cases.body: Please take me off this list, I don't want any more of these emails.
cases.notes: failure mode: prose opt-out — no carrier keyword, so the deterministic pass correctly declines and the model must catch it

cases.body: remove me from your mailing list please
cases.notes: failure mode: prose opt-out

cases.body: Please cancel my order #10041, but keep sending me the newsletter — I like it.
cases.notes: failure mode: keyword-in-prose — contains CANCEL and is emphatically NOT an opt-out; this case is why detectOptOut matches the whole message and not a substring

cases.body: I'd rather not get the promo texts any more but the order updates are fine.
cases.notes: failure mode: partial opt-out — a category-scoped preference; suppression is address-level so this must reach a human, not an automatic suppression
